meta.what: Payments to Russia for weapons, military equipment and military services (incl. spares, licence kits, repair, training), by buyer country and year. Payments (cash or offsets) received by Russia, not SIPRI TIV.
meta.units: EUR bn nominal per year; 2026 = January-August, not annualised. USD converted with ECB annual averages (USD per EUR): 2019 1.11947, 2020 1.14219, 2021 1.18274, 2022 1.05304, 2023 1.08126, 2024 1.08238, 2025 1.12998, 2026 1.16285 (2026 = Jan-Aug mean).
meta.method: (1) National total per year from Russian official statements (FSVTS/Putin/Rostec): ~15 (2019), >15 (2020), 14.6 (2021), ~7 (2022), ~6 (2023), claim 13.75 (2024) vs Rostec "lower than 6", claim >15 (2025); central path 15.0/15.5/14.6/7.1/6.0/6.5/9.0/6.6 USD bn (2026 Jan-Aug). (2) Allocation to buyers from contract reporting, SIPRI recipient shares (2017-21, 2019-23, 2020-24, 2021-25) and payment timing (advances, stuck payments), with a residual "ROW". (3) Ranges per country: multipliers on the central value (wider for certainty D). (4) expected_no_war: what the buyer would have paid per year without the war, given the pre-war contract pipeline and the pre-war decline that SIPRI documents for 2020-21 (one-offs like Turkey's S-400 removed). (5) change = expected - actual: positive = less paid to Russia (toward Ukraine), negative = more paid (toward Russia). Ranges of the change combine baseline and actual half-ranges in quadrature. (6) in_customs: the part of the payments that is already inside the buyer's imports from Russia in trade_full.json (checked against UN Comtrade HS 88/89/93/8411/8526/8710/8805/8906 lines, partner Russia).
meta.recommended_use: Add "paid to Russia for arms" as its own part using change_vs_expected_ex_customs (central; range = central shifted by the change_vs_expected half-ranges). It removes the in_customs part, whose change already sits in trade_full. Use prewar_avg_2019_2021 only as an alternative; it overstates the cut (one-offs, pre-war decline). Show not_buyer_choice_share as a label (like sanctions_share).

IND.name: India

expected_no_war_per_year.note: USD bn/yr (3.5, 2.5, 4.5) converted at ~1.10; per-year conversion used in change

not_buyer_choice_share.note: share of the fall due to Russian supply limits (war priority, sanctions on production) or pre-war trend, not the buyer's choice; label only

IND.note: Largest buyer (SIPRI: 48% of Russian major-arms deliveries 2021-25). S-400 (USD 5.43bn, 2018; 3 of 5 regiments by 2023, rest 2026-27), two Project 11356 frigates (Tushil Dec 2024, Tamal Jul 2025), Chakra III lease, AK-203 JV, Su-30MKI/T-90 licence kits, AL-31FP kits for HAL, spares. India paid ~USD 5.4-5.9bn/yr to all foreign vendors (Lok Sabha, FY2019-22); Russia ~45-60% of that plus licence kits. Over USD 2bn of payments stuck for ~a year (Bloomberg Apr 2023) -> low 2022-23, catch-up later.

customs_check.IND: India reported imports from Russia: HS 93 USD 0.0-22m/yr, HS 88 USD 0.5-24m, HS 89 USD 6-35m except 2020 (HS 8906 USD 346m, a vessel), HS 8411 <5m. India's capital acquisitions from Russia (S-400, frigates) are not in DGCI&S customs data. HS 99 (unspecified) USD 0.25-0.92bn/yr from Russia could hide some items: high case.
customs_check.CHN: China reported HS 8411 imports from Russia USD 12-17m (2019-21) vs Russia's reported 8411 exports to China USD 1.57-1.77bn: military engines are missing from China's data. HS 88 USD 68-154m (mostly helicopter/aircraft parts) partly civil.
customs_check.DZA: No Algerian report 2019-23 (trade_full uses Russia's mirror 2019-21 = HS 93 USD 63m in 2019, HS 8411 1-77m, and IMF 2022-23); 2024 own report includes HS 8805 USD 179m and HS 8526 USD 200m.
customs_check.KAZ: HS 8802 aircraft from Russia USD 61-222m/yr; assumed ~30% military.
customs_check.TUR: No S-400 visible in HS 93/88/8710; Turkish customs likely excludes it. High case 0.5 for 2019.
customs_check.note: Russia's own customs data (FCS) excludes arms exported under military-technical cooperation; only civil/dual items like HS 8411 engines appear.

overlaps: (a) trade_full.json (goods imports from Russia): arms are almost entirely outside buyers' customs data; the in_customs series gives the part that is inside (central about EUR 0.1-0.5bn/yr in total, mostly Algeria 2024, Kazakhstan, Serbia, India 2020). Subtract in_customs change from this part, or equivalently use (payments - in_customs). (b) flowback2.json / other.json military_to_russia: the opposite direction (Iran, North Korea, Belarus, China supplying Russia). Iran: if Su-35s are partly paid by drones/missiles delivered to Russia, counting both double counts that barter value (up to EUR 1-2bn); Iran's high case here assumes cash. (c) china_military.json: China to Russia, other direction; no overlap. (d) services (BaTiS/Eurostat): repair/training of Russian-made equipment could appear in partners' services imports from Russia (maintenance and repair, government goods and services n.i.e.); likely small, most partners (India, China, Algeria) are BaTiS-modelled. (e) companies_all.json: Vietnam's arms payments via Rusvietpetro are dividends forgone, not taxes; no overlap with company taxes. (f) residual.json (Russia's import gap) is about Russia's imports, not exports; no overlap.
notes: Official Russian totals are "foreign-currency revenue" and include advances on new contracts; independent analysts doubt the 2024 and 2025 claims, so the national path used is well below them in 2024-2025 and the high cases reach them. Jamestown/Arbat figures of USD 3bn (2023) and <1bn (2024) are SIPRI TIV mislabelled as dollars and are not used. Most of the fall since 2022 is not the buyers' choice: Rostec and SIPRI attribute it to Russia prioritising its own army, sanctions and US pressure (CAATSA); the not_buyer_choice_share label reflects that. Egypt, Indonesia, Turkey and partly India cut orders under US pressure (buyer choice, but sanctions-driven). Rest-of-world (ROW) is not attributed to ISO3 codes.
